operation_details.item: The user prefers long contextual introductions and broad motivation paragraphs in conference abstracts before stating results, even under tight word limits.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How is the conference abstract coming along for the June submission? I know the word limit is unusually tight this year.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: It is taking shape. I’m resisting the urge to lead with the findings—I prefer opening with a fairly broad motivation and enough context to show why the problem matters before stating the results.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense for positioning the work. Are you planning to connect the motivation to the wider literature as well as the immediate project?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, briefly. Even under a strict word limit, I’d rather preserve a substantial introductory paragraph and trim procedural details before cutting the broader scholarly framing.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That will give readers a clearer reason to care before they reach the technical section. Has the lab team finished checking the results you’ll report?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: The lab coordinator is consolidating the final checks today. I’m also revising a grant narrative and trying to keep the same emphasis on context, motivation, and the contribution rather than rushing straight to claims.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: A consistent narrative should help across both documents. Are you presenting the abstract at the conference, or will someone else from the group handle the lecture?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’ll give the lecture myself. I’m scheduling the travel and checking whether the department can cover the registration and poster-printing costs before I finalize everything.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For conference abstracts, I want long contextual introductions with broad motivation paragraphs before stating results, even when the word limit is tight.
